sources.entry: Ruby: _Creating a Linux Desktop application with Ruby_

summary.title: Creating a GTK ToDo Application with Ruby
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simple desktop ToDo app in Ruby using the gtk3 gem, Glade-designed UI templates, GResource bundling, and JSON-file storage.
keywords: how to make a gtk app with ruby
takeaways: Install the gtk3 Ruby gem and Glade, then create a Gtk::Application subclass with a signal-driven activate handler.
Design UI in Glade as a composite template, pack it into a binary GResource with glib-compile-resources, and load it in Ruby.
Bind template children (such as buttons) to a custom Gtk::ApplicationWindow subclass with bind_template_child.
Persist ToDo items as JSON files in a hidden folder in the home directory, with a Todo::Item model handling save, load and delete.
summary.summary: This tutorial by Lazarus Lazaridis walks through building a simple ToDo desktop application in Ruby using the gtk3 gem (GTK+ Ruby bindings). It sets up the project structure, a Gtk::Application subclass, and automatic loading of Ruby files. UI is designed in Glade, saved as an XML template, compiled into a binary GResource with glib-compile-resources, and bound to a custom window class. The post also introduces a JSON-file-backed Todo::Item model and starts wiring an Add button to a new-item window; the page ends mid-tutorial in the Glade layout steps.
